# T3.8 public shopper page, redacted transcript.
#
# Provenance: the run's raw console output was never committed — its drive
# script stayed outside the repo, as T3.7's did — so there is no capture to
# redact. Nothing below was re-run for this file. It reassembles what the
# tree still carries, and every line says which: a "note" line quotes
# T3.8's committed notes (dev-diary/PHASE-3-agent.md); a "page" line is the
# served artifact's own committed text (public/index.html) or this
# package's spec (astropods.yml); a "code" line is what server/index.ts
# does, read from the tree.
#
# Placeholders: <frontend-host>, <chat-host>, <deployment-id>, <build-page>,
# <trace-id>, <conv-id>, <client-id>, <sso-state>, <user-id>. Spend amounts
# kept, as in testdata/astropods/15-public-probe.txt. No key and no account
# detail: the drive script held the CLI login token in process memory and
# never printed it.

## Deployment (probe-gw only; memento-agent untouched throughout)

note: the page is served from probe-gw, not memento-agent. That deployment
      has no frontend host (messaging only) and its access is not public, so
      it cannot serve judges. No access switch was flipped by this task:
      Public is the user's console control, and the CLI offers none.
note: F3 shape — the shopper frontend is a separate deployment with its own
      spec in agent/frontend/ (astropods.yml, Dockerfile, server/, public/),
      pushed and redeployed on probe-gw; agent/runtime/ was read, never
      edited, and memento-agent still runs its original build.
page: agent.interfaces = {frontend: true, messaging: true}; one container
      serves the page and /health on the injected PORT (80 in production)
      and registers messaging through serve().
page: Dockerfile stays ROOT with EXPOSE 80 (the T3.7 proven shape). The
      change that would be needed if the page ever moves onto the reference
      agent is recorded in T3.8's notes, not made here.

## Anonymous page check (fresh session, browser UA, no cookies, no key)

     https://<frontend-host>/          -> 200, no redirect, the shopper page
     https://<frontend-host>/health    -> 200, from the container
     https://<frontend-host>/<unknown> -> 404, from the container
     https://<chat-host>/              -> 302 to the platform SSO
# note: "Anonymous evidence (fresh session, browser UA): GET / on the
# frontend host 200 with no redirect serving the shopper page (proof trace
# baked in); /health 200 from the container; unknown path 404 from the
# container; chat host still 302 to the platform SSO."
# page: the served page is public/index.html — <title>Memento Emptor —
# shopper page</title>, h1 "Memento Emptor — shopper page", the flow list
# (recall, recommend, correct, approve) and the "Try it" prompts.
# The 404 is the container's own fallback (code: fetch -> "not found"), so
# no SSO appears on any path of the frontend host.

## Standing configuration on the deployment

note: the agent answers from the recorded demo fixture (same ids and words
      the reference agent replays, seeded marks shown); live corrections
      persist in container memory only and reset on redeploy (the demo
      reset); at most 30 model turns per container lifetime, then an honest
      429; approval is an explicit yes with no purchase tool on this page.
code: those last two are server/relay.ts's turn budget (MAX_TURNS) and the
      page's tool list; relay.test.ts now holds them, so an edit that drops
      the cap or loosens the request shape fails the gate.

## What this file is not

It is not a capture. The one thing it cannot supply is the byte-exact CLI
output of the run; what it supplies is the result, in the shape T3.7's
probe records its own: which hosts answered what, what each turn cost, the
proof turn's id, and the configuration the deployment was left in.
